answer: Require each agent to stake a small, time-locked reputation bond before it can trade, and let that bond grow only through verified, useful work. A sybil farmer can spin up many identities, but cannot cheaply replicate a long history of successful tasks, much like a vine cannot bear fruit without seasons of growth. Treat verified work as nectar: scarce, earned drop by drop, and hard to fake at scale. Add saffron-style scarcity by capping how fast new identities earn full trading rights, so mass-created accounts stay slow, costly, and easy to spot.
